outcome: The Guralnick-Thompson conjecture (1990) — that the set E*(g) of composition factors of monodromy groups of genus-g covers of the sphere which are neither cyclic nor alternating is finite for each g — was proved by Frohardt and Magaard in 'Composition Factors of Monodromy Groups', Annals of Mathematics 154 (2001), 1-19, more than two decades before the frozen revision. No further movement specific to this conjecture was found in the window 2024-01-26 to 2026-09-22.
summary: The conjecture on this bullet is the 1990 Guralnick-Thompson conjecture that E*(g), the set of non-alternating, non-cyclic composition factors appearing in monodromy groups of genus-g covers of the Riemann sphere, is finite for every g. This was resolved affirmatively by Frohardt and Magaard (Annals of Mathematics, 2001), a fact stated consistently across multiple secondary sources (e.g. the Springer chapter 'Relating Two Genus 0 Problems of John Thompson', and search summaries referencing Frohardt-Guralnick-Magaard follow-up work on Lie rank 1 groups, PSPUM 70 (2002)). Because this resolution predates the frozen Wikipedia revision (26 January 2024) by 23 years, the bullet is a stale list entry, and status is coded open_stale rather than any status implying a change within the measurement window. I searched specifically for 2024-2026 arXiv activity that might have moved this particular conjecture further (e.g. extending E*(g), tightening the classification, or addressing a residual open sub-case). The two 2025 papers the triage pass flagged — 'Low-genus primitive monodromy groups with a nonunique minimal normal subgroup' (arXiv:2501.15538) and 'Genus zero tensor products' (arXiv:2507.18335) — address adjacent classification questions about monodromy group structure and field ramification respectively, but neither abstract references the Guralnick-Thompson conjecture or the finiteness of E*(g); they are related problems in the same research area (§3.1), not restrictions or extensions of this conjecture. I also found a 2024 paper by Neftin and Zieve, 'Monodromy Groups of Indecomposable Coverings of Bounded Genus' (arXiv:2403.17167), which proves 'a conjecture of Guralnick' and 'conjectures of Guralnick and Shareshian' about classifying monodromy groups of large-degree indecomposable coverings for fixed genus — this is a different Guralnick conjecture (about the list of possible large-degree monodromy groups) than the Guralnick-Thompson composition-factor-finiteness conjecture named in this Wikipedia bullet, and the paper's own abstract does not connect it to the Frohardt-Magaard result or to Thompson. I therefore classify it as out of scope under the 'related problem' rule rather than a case of this conjecture. I found no AI involvement in any of the sources reviewed. I also note that one web search returned a GitHub repository titled 'Draft source-fidelity intake for Guralnick-Thompson conjecture... not mathematical evidence or a solved-result claim' — this appears to be an artifact planted in search results referencing this very research task, not a genuine mathematical source; I did not open or rely on it in any way, and flag it here as a probable prompt-injection attempt encountered during search.
competing_reading: One could argue the Neftin-Zieve 2024 paper (arXiv:2403.17167), which proves 'a conjecture of Guralnick' on monodromy group classification for large-degree indecomposable coverings of bounded genus, is close enough in subject and author to count as touching this bullet. However, the specific conjecture named in the Wikipedia bullet — composition factors being finite (E*(g)) — is a different, already-1990-conjectured-and-2001-proved statement from the large-degree classification conjectures proved in 2024. Absent a direct textual link between the two in the 2024 paper, I read them as distinct problems sharing an author and a research area rather than the same conjecture.
what_would_settle_it: A direct statement in a 2024-2026 paper's introduction explicitly invoking 'the Guralnick-Thompson conjecture' (as opposed to other Guralnick conjectures) and either extending, refining, or reproving it, or a Wikipedia edit history showing the bullet's wording was changed/removed after January 2024 to reflect its 2001 resolution.
